  out: '=== #171 Shortcut tests fail when shortcut.test.ts and repo-issue-edit.test.ts share a vitest worker\n' +
    '## Problem\n' +
    '\n' +
    "`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` and `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.test.ts` fail whenever vitest puts them in the same worker, and pass when it doesn't. Which files share a worker changes between runs, so the failure looks random.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '**Root cause.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `isolate: false`, so test files in one worker share modules and the same `document`. Both files call `initGlobalShortcut()` (`repo-issue-edit.test.ts` at module level, `shortcut.test.ts` in `beforeAll`). Each call adds two more `keydown` listeners to `document`, and they all dispatch into the same shared `globalRegistry`. After the second call, every key press runs its shortcut twice.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**How I know:**\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- CI: the `sonarqube` job on #161 failed with `repo-issue-edit.test.ts &gt; r quotes the selection after the existing text, or only moves to the reply box`: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times` (`moveCursorToEnd`, line 78). Run: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43088279012/job/130770579133. In the same commit\'s `frontend` job, that file passed. #161 doesn\'t change either test file or `shortcut.ts`, which are identical to `main`.\n' +
    '- Locally, forcing both files into one worker fails every time, in either order:\n' +
    '  ```bash\n' +
    '  pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.test.ts --no-file-parallelism\n' +
    '  ```\n' +
    '  One order fails `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` (1 test) and the other fails `shortcut.test.ts` (3 tests).\n' +
    '- Adding a temporary "already initialized" guard to `initGlobalShortcut()` makes the same command pass.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Why it also breaks SonarCloud.** The `sonarqube` job runs vitest with coverage before the scan. When a test fails, vitest writes no `coverage/lcov.info`, so Sonar sees every new TypeScript line as uncovered (`new_coverage 0.0 &lt; 80`) and the quality gate fails. That can happen on any PR, whatever it changes.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## Goal\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The two files pass regardless of order or worker grouping, and a page that calls `initGlobalShortcut()` more than once still runs each shortcut once per key press.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## Acceptance Criteria\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- [ ] AC1: Given both files run in one worker (command above), when the run finishes, then all tests in both files pass, in both orders.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC2: Given `initGlobalShortcut()` has been called twice, when a registered shortcut key is pressed once, then its action runs exactly once (new unit test).\n' +
    '- [ ] AC3: Given the fix is in, when the full frontend suite (`pnpm exec vitest run`) runs\n' +

    '=== #151 Code suggestions in pull request reviews\n' +
    '### User Story\n' +
    '\n' +
    "As a reviewer, I want to suggest an exact code change in a review comment, and as the PR author, I want to apply it with one click, so that small fixes don't need to be explained and retyped.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '### User Scenario\n' +
    '\n' +
    'A reviewer selects a few lines in a pull request diff and writes the code she would like to see instead. The PR author sees her suggestion as a diff in the conversation, clicks to apply it, and Gitea adds a commit with that change to the PR branch.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Acceptance Criteria\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The criteria below are a starting point and are incomplete. The open questions must be answered before implementation.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- [ ] AC1: Given selected lines in a PR diff, when a reviewer adds a suggestion, then the comment shows the suggested change as a diff.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC2: Given a suggestion, when the PR author applies it, then a commit with the change is added to the PR branch.\n' +
    "- [ ] AC3: Given a user who can't push to the PR branch, when they try to apply a suggestion, then nothing is committed and they see why.\n" +
    '- [ ] More criteria needed, based on the open questions below.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Acceptance criteria should also cover invalid input, failures, conflicts, and permissions, not only the main path.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Out of Scope\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- Suggestions on commits outside a pull request\n' +
    '- Suggestions that create, rename, or delete files\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Open Questions\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- What happens if the code changed after the suggestion was made?\n' +
    '- Who besides the PR author may apply a suggestion? What about pull requests from forks?\n' +
    '- What if the PR is closed or merged, or its branch was deleted?\n' +
    '- Can several suggestions be applied at once? What if they touch the same lines?\n' +
    '- Who appears as the author of the commit?\n' +
    '- What happens if two people apply suggestions at the same time?\n' +
    '- Can suggestions be applied through the API?\n' +
    '- What happens to existing data and installations after upgrading?\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Design Decision\n' +
    '\n' +
    'To be filled in before implementation.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Decision:**\n' +
    '**Alternatives Considered:**\n' +
    '**Rationale:**\n' +
    '**Consequences:**\n' +
    '\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Scope\n' +
    '\n' +
    'large\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Scope Justification\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Review comments and their markdown rendering, the PR diff UI, creating commits on the PR branch, permissions, and the API.\n' +

    '=== #102 Subscribe to one personal deadline feed across all my repositories\n' +
    '### User Story\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #36 · Depends on C\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## User Story\n' +
    'As a developer who works across several repositories, I want a single calendar feed of the\n' +
    'deadlines on issues assigned to me and the milestones in my repositories, so that I subscribe\n' +
    'once instead of once per repository.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### User Scenario\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Sam is assigned issues in five repositories. Under **Settings → Applications → Calendar token**\n' +
    'he copies the "All my deadlines" URL, `/sam/deadlines.ics?token=cal_…`, and adds it to his\n' +
    'calendar. His assigned issue deadlines from all five repos show up with the repo name in each\n' +
    'title. When he is unassigned from one issue, it drops off the feed on the next refresh.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Acceptance Criteria\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- [ ] AC1: Given a valid calendar token for user `sam`, when `/sam/deadlines.ics?token=…` is\n' +
    '  fetched, then it returns one VEVENT for each open issue with a deadline assigned to `sam` in a\n' +
    '  repository he can read, with titles prefixed by `owner/repo`.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC2: Given a token that belongs to a different user, or no token, when\n' +
    '  `/sam/deadlines.ics` is fetched, then it returns `404`.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC3: Given that Sam loses access to a repository, when the feed is fetched again, then that\n' +
    "  repository's issues are no longer in it.\n" +
    "- [ ] AC4: Given an issue that also appears in that repository's own `issues.ics`, when both\n" +
    '  feeds are compared, then the event has the same `UID` in both, so a client subscribed to both\n' +
    '  feeds shows it once.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC5: Given more matching issues than the cap from issue B, when the feed is fetched, then\n' +
    '  it returns at most the cap.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Out of Scope\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- A cross-repository in-app `/calendar` page (follow-up once A ships).\n' +
    '- Including issues the user created or is watching but is not assigned to.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Open Questions\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- Should milestones of every repository the user can write to be included, or only issues\n' +
    '  assigned to them? (Proposed: assigned issues only, to keep the query bounded.)\n' +
    '\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Design Decision\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Decision:** Build the feed from one `IssuesOptions` query with `AssigneeID = user`, the #34\n' +
    '`HasDeadline` filter and the repository access condition the user dashboard already uses. Render\n' +
    'it with the serializer from issue B, so UIDs match the per-repo feeds.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Alternatives Considered:**\n' +
    '- *Merge the per-repo feeds in Go.* This makes one query per repository, which is slow for users\n' +
    '  in many repos, and it is hard to cap the total size.\n' +
    '- *Let the client subscribe to each repo feed (do nothing\n' +

    '=== #101 Subscribe to private repository calendar feeds with a revocable calendar token\n' +
    '### User Story\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #36 · Depends on B\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## User Story\n' +
    'As a member of a private repository, I want a calendar subscription URL that works without\n' +
    'signing in but only exposes calendar data and can be revoked, so that I can follow private\n' +
    'deadlines in my calendar app without pasting a full-power access token into a third-party service.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### User Scenario\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Lena works on the private repo `acme/backend`. On its milestones page she clicks "Subscribe\n' +
    '(iCal)". A dialog explains that the URL contains a personal calendar token and shows\n' +
    '`https://gitea.example/acme/backend/milestones.ics?token=cal_…`. She adds it to Outlook. Later she\n' +
    'pastes the URL by mistake into a shared calendar. She goes to **Settings → Applications →\n' +
    'Calendar token** and clicks "Regenerate", and the old URL stops working at once. When she leaves\n' +
    'the `acme` organization, her feed stops returning `acme/backend` events on its next fetch.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Acceptance Criteria\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- [ ] AC1: Given a signed-in user, when they open **Settings → Applications**, then they can\n' +
    '  create, view, regenerate or delete one calendar token. Only a hash is stored, and the plain\n' +
    '  token is shown once, when it is created.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC2: Given a valid calendar token in the `token` query parameter, when it is sent to an\n' +
    '  `.ics` route of a private repo the token owner can read, then the feed is returned with\n' +
    '  `Cache-Control: private`.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC3: Given the same calendar token, when it is sent to any non-`.ics` route (an\n' +
    '  API endpoint, an RSS feed, or a repo page), then it does not authenticate the request.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC4: Given a personal access token, when it is sent as `?token=` to an `.ics` route, then\n' +
    '  it is rejected. Personal access tokens never authenticate calendar feeds.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC5: Given a token whose owner has lost read access to the repository, when the feed is\n' +
    '  fetched, then it returns `404`. Access is checked on every request, not when the token is\n' +
    '  created.\n' +
    '- [ ] AC6: Given a token that has been regenerated or deleted, when the old URL is fetched, then\n' +
    '  it returns `404`.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Out of Scope\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- Tokens limited to one repository, or tokens with expiry dates (possible follow-ups).\n' +
    '- The cross-repository user feed (issue D).\n' +
    "- Admin pages that list or revoke other users' calendar tokens.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '### Open Questions\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- Should a bad token return `401` or `404`? (Proposed: `404`, so the response does not reveal that\n' +
    '  a private repo exists.)\n' +
    '- Should the token be removed automatica\n' +

    '=== #37 Expedite integration test suite\n' +
    '### What problem would this solve?\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Summary**\n' +
    "The integration suite takes roughly 25–30 minutes for a full pass, so in practice almost nobody runs it before pushing; contributors push, wait on CI, and find out later. A run on 2026-09-14 consumed the default 10-minute `go test` timeout having completed about 252 of 700 top-level tests. Individual tests run far over the project's own target of sub-2s: thirteen exceeded 10 seconds, and two dominate — `TestActionsScopedWorkflows` at 1m17s and `TestActionsReusableWorkflow` at 50s, both single large blocks whose cost is fixture setup and git I/O rather than assertions. Nothing holds the line today: no budget, no ratchet, and no signal short of the whole CI job timing out.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '**User story**\n' +
    '"As a contributor, I want to run the integration tests relevant to my change and get an answer in under a minute so that I can iterate locally instead of using CI as my test runner."\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Rough scope — Large**\n' +
    'Establishing which tests are parallel-safe is itself undocumented groundwork, and the work then spans the test harness, CI configuration, fixture design, and a new enforcement mechanism.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Source**\n' +
    'Analysis of a full `go test ./...` run of this fork on 2026-09-14, measured against the sub-2s target in `AGENTS.md`.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### What do you propose?\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Solution proposal**\n' +
    'Make the suite something developers actually run:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- **Establish which tests are parallel-safe.** The rule separating tests that tolerate `t.Parallel()` from those needing serial DB state is currently written down nowhere. Document it, then enable parallelism where it is safe. This is groundwork for everything else here.\n' +
    '- **Sharding**, so CI can fan out across N workers and a developer can run a single shard locally.\n' +
    '- **Selective runs** targeting the area you changed, rather than all-or-nothing.\n' +
    '- **An enforced runtime budget.** The test logger already emits `+++ TestX is a slow test (run: …)` lines, so the data exists — turn it into a report, set a per-test ceiling, and fail CI on regressions past it.\n' +
    '- **Faster fixtures for the worst offenders.** Share repository fixtures across subtests in the two Actions tests instead of creating one per `t.Run`, and split them into independently runnable tests. Profile first to confirm setup is the cost rather than the `FlushAll(ctx, 5*time.Second)` calls.\n' +
    '- **Make standard tooling work.** A bare `go test ./...` currently dies at the 10-minute default with a goroutine dump and no failing assertion, because the 40-minute tim\n' +

    '=== #36 Calendar view and iCalendar subscription feed\n' +
    '### What problem would this solve?\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Summary**\n' +
    'Deadlines in Gitea live only inside Gitea. There is no calendar view, and no way to get dates into the calendar a developer keeps open all day — Gitea publishes RSS and Atom feeds for activity but has no iCalendar support anywhere in the codebase. A team that sets milestone due dates has to re-enter them by hand in Google Calendar or Outlook, and the copies drift the first time a date moves.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**User story**\n' +
    "As a developer, I want my repository's milestones and issue deadlines in the calendar I already use, updating automatically, so that project dates sit alongside the rest of my schedule instead of somewhere I have to remember to check.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '**Rough scope — Large**\n' +
    'The calendar view is routine, but private-repository feeds need revocable calendar-scoped tokens in the URL — calendar clients cannot do OAuth — and that security design is the part most likely to expand.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Source**\n' +

```text
=== #156 OPEN CarsonRackley Sprint 3 S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch
Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned the way Gitea's other web forms return them: HTTP 400 with
the message shown on the page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on a single line, in a review comment or a reply in its thread, and
  a user who can push to the head branch, when they apply it, then exactly one commit is added to
  the head branch that replaces only that line, exactly as #154's diff shows it (AC12). The form
  is prefilled with the default message "Apply suggestion from @&lt;reviewer&gt; on &lt;file&gt;" and can be
  edited: the commit uses the submitted message, or the default if the message is submitted
  empty.
- [ ] AC2: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without
  "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a
  direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing (#151 AC3). A signed-out viewer sees no Apply
  button, and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing. *Pending customer question 2
  on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*
- [ ] AC3: Given the commented line's text at the current head differs from the line the
  suggestion was written against, or the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number
  is now past the end of the file, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see
  "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given the head branch moved between page load and Apply (someone pushed, or another
  suggestion was applied), when Apply is submitted with the old head SHA, then nothing is
  committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the page was loaded. Reload the page
  and try again." This holds whether or not the new commits touched the suggestion's file. The
  head SHA sent is the PR's head when the page loaded, even when the Files tab is showing a single
  earlier commit.
- [ ] AC5: Given the PR is closed or merged, its he
OUT OF SCOPE: Out of Scope

- Several suggestions at once (S6); API (S7); recording "applied" state (S4).
- Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines (customer question 5): they render as plain code blocks
  in #154, so there is nothing to apply. If the customer allows them, that's a follow-up issue.
- Resolving the review conversation on apply (customer question 3).
- Applying without JavaScript: like #154's no-JavaScript fallback, the suggestion is then a plain
  code block with no Apply button.
- Suggestions spanning several commented lines (S5). A one-line comment whose block has several
  lines is in scope (AC12).
- AGit-flow pull requests (pushed to `refs/for/...`): there is no head branch to commit to, so they
  get no Apply button (AC5).
```

```text
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	unit_model "gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"
	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMilestoneBurndown(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	t.Run("Data", func(t *testing.T) {
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)

		due := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, 7)
		req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones", api.CreateMilestoneOption{
			Title: "burndown", Deadline: &amp;due,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		milestone := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &amp;api.Milestone{})

		indexes := make([]int64, 0, 2)
		for _, title := range []string{"first", "second"} {
			req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{
				Title: title, Milestone: milestone.ID,
			}).AddTokenAuth(token)
			indexes = append(indexes, DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &amp;api.Issue{}).Index)
		}
		closed := "closed"
		req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", indexes[0]), api.EditIssueOption{
			State: &amp;closed,
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)

		// anyone who can read the repository's issues can read its burndown
		req = NewRequest(t, "GET", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/milestone/%d/burndown", milestone.ID))
		burndown := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &amp;issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})

		// one day of history, or two if the test ran across midnight; too few to project either way
		require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points)
		require.LessOrEqual(t, len(burndown.Points), 2)
		today := burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Remaining)
		assert.Equal(t, 2, today.Scope)
		assert.Equal(t, issue_service.BurndownInsufficientData, burndown.Status)
		require.NotNil(t, burndown.Ideal)
		assert.Equal(t, burndown.Points[0].Date, burndown.Ideal.From)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, burndown.Ideal.FromValue)
		assert.Equal(t, burndown.Deadline, burndown.Ideal.To)

		// the chart and the progress bar above it must count the same thing
		row := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &amp;issues_model.Milestone{ID: milestone.ID})
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues-row.NumClosedIssues, today.Remaining)
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues, today.Scope)
	})

	t.Run("RealLifecycle", func(t *testing.T) {
		// close, reopen and move through the API, so the history the chart replays is written by the
		// real code paths rather than built by hand as in the unit tests
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)
		createMilestone := func(title string) int64 {
			req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/milestones", api.CreateMilestoneOption{Title: title}).AddTokenAuth(token)
			return DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &amp;api.Milestone{}).ID
		}
		sprint, other := createMilestone("sprint"), createMilestone("other")

		issues := map[string]*api.Issue{}
		for _, title := range []string{"closed", "reopened", "moved", "open"} {
			req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{Title: title, Milestone: sprint}).AddTokenAuth(token)
			issues[title] = DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &amp;api.Issue{})
		}
		edit := func(title string, option api.EditIssueOption) {
			req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", issues[title].Index), option).AddTokenAuth(token)
			MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)
		}
		closed, open := "closed", "open"
		edit("closed", api.EditIssueOption{State: &amp;closed})
		edit("reopened", api.EditIssueOption{State: &amp;closed})
		edit("reopened", api.EditIssueOption{State: &amp;open})
		edit("moved", api.EditIssueOption{Milestone: &amp;other})

		// the reconciliation step would hide missing history in the final counts, so check the
		// history itself: four joins, one move out, two closes and one reopen
		scopeEvents, err := issues_model.GetMilestoneScopeEvents(t.Context(), 1, sprint)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		var joins, leaves int
		for _, e := range scopeEvents {
			if e.MilestoneID == sprint {
				joins++
			} else if e.OldMilestoneID == sprint {
				leaves++
				assert.Equal(t, issues["moved"].ID, e.IssueID)
			}
		}
		assert.Equal(t, 4, joins)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, leaves)

		ids := []int64{issues["closed"].ID, issues["reopened"].ID, issues["moved"].ID, issues["open"].ID}
		stateEvents, err := issues_model.GetMilestoneStateEvents(t.Context(), ids)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		kinds := make([]issues_model.CommentType, 0, len(stateEvents))
		for _, e := range stateEvents {
			kinds = append(kinds, e.Type)
		}
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []issues_model.CommentType{issues_model.CommentTypeClose, issues_model.CommentTypeClose, issues_model.CommentTypeReopen}, kinds)

		read := func(milestoneID int64) issue_service.BurndownPoint {
			req := NewRequest(t, "GET", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/milestone/%d/burndown", milestoneID))
			burndown := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &amp;issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})
			require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points)
			return burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
		}
		// "closed", "reopened" and "open" are left; only the latter two are open
		today := read(sprint)
		assert.Equal(t, 3, today.Scope)
		assert.Equal(t, 2, today.Remaining)
		row := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &amp;issues_model.Milestone{ID: sprint})
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues, today.Scope)
		assert.Equal(t, row.NumIssues-row.NumClosedIssues, today.Remaining)

		// today's list names each close and reopen; the move out happened on the milestone's first
		// day of work, which is never marked as a change of scope
		var changes []string
		for _, c := range today.Changes {
			changes = append(changes, fmt.Sprintf("%s #%d %s", c.Kind, c.Index, c.Title))
		}
		assert.Equal(t, []string{
			fmt.Sprintf("closed #%d closed", issues["closed"].Index),
			fmt.Sprintf("closed #%d reopened", issues["reopened"].Index),
			fmt.Sprintf("reopened #%d reopened", issues["reopened"].Index),
		}, changes)

		// the moved issue now counts in the milestone it went to
		today = read(other)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Scope)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Remaining)
	})

	t.Run("PullRequestsOnRequest", func(t *testing.T) {
		// milestone 1 holds pull request #2 and nothing else, has no creation time, and is due in the
		// year 9999: issues only by default, so it charts nothing until pull requests are asked for
		req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown")
		burndown := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &amp;issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})
		assert.Equal(t, issue_service.BurndownEmpty, burndown.Status)
		assert.Empty(t, burndown.Points)

		req = NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown?include_pulls=1")
		burndown = DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &amp;issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})
		require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points)
		today := burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Scope)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Remaining)
		assert.Nil(t, burndown.Ideal)
		assert.Empty(t, burndown.Deadline)
	})

	t.Run("NotFound", func(t *testing.T) {
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestone/99999/burndown"), http.StatusNotFound)
		// milestone 4 belongs to repo 42, so it cannot be read through repo 1
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestone/4/burndown"), http.StatusNotFound)
	})

	t.Run("PrivateRepoHidden", func(t *testing.T) {
		// user2/repo2 is private, so a signed-out reader learns nothing about its milestones
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo2/milestone/1/burndown"), http.StatusNotFound)
	})
}

// milestoneWithClosedIssue adds a closed issue to milestone 1 of user2/repo1, which already holds
// pull request #2, so the chart has one item of each kind and the issue appears in today's changes
func milestoneWithClosedIssue(t *testing.T) *api.Issue {
	token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, loginUser(t, "user2"), auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteIssue)
	req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, "POST", "/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues", api.CreateIssueOption{
		Title: "only for issue readers", Milestone: 1,
	}).AddTokenAuth(token)
	created := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated), &amp;api.Issue{})
	closed := "closed"
	req = NewRequestWithJSON(t, "PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/issues/%d", created.Index), api.EditIssueOption{
		State: &amp;closed,
	}).AddTokenAuth(token)
	MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusCreated)
	return created
}

func readBurndown(t *testing.T, url string) *issue_service.MilestoneBurndown {
	return DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusOK), &amp;issue_service.MilestoneBurndown{})
}

func TestMilestoneBurndownWithoutPullAccess(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	created := milestoneWithClosedIssue(t)
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &amp;repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	require.NoError(t, repo_service.UpdateRepositoryUnits(t.Context(), repo, nil, []unit_model.Type{unit_model.TypePullRequests}))

	// asking for pull requests cannot count one the viewer may not read
	burndown := readBurndown(t, "/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown?include_pulls=1")
	require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points)
	today := burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
	assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Scope, "the issue only")
	for _, c := range today.Changes {
		assert.False(t, c.IsPull)
	}
	require.Len(t, today.Changes, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, created.Index, today.Changes[0].Index)
}

func TestMilestoneBurndownWithoutIssueAccess(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	created := milestoneWithClosedIssue(t)
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &amp;repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	require.NoError(t, repo_service.UpdateRepositoryUnits(t.Context(), repo, nil, []unit_model.Type{unit_model.TypeIssues}))

	// a pull request reader still reaches the milestone and sees its pull requests by default, rather
	// than an "empty" chart; the closed issue is never counted or listed, asked for or not
	for _, url := range []string{"/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown", "/user2/repo1/milestone/1/burndown?include_pulls=1"} {
		burndown := readBurndown(t, url)
		require.NotEmpty(t, burndown.Points, url)
		today := burndown.Points[len(burndown.Points)-1]
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Scope, "the pull request only: %s", url)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, today.Remaining, url)
		for _, p := range burndown.Points {
			for _, c := range p.Changes {
				assert.NotEqual(t, created.Index, c.Index, "an unreadable issue leaked into %s of %s", p.Date, url)
			}
		}
	}
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestRepoCalendar(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	defer timeutil.MockSet(time.Date(2026, 10, 7, 12, 0, 0, 0, setting.DefaultUILocation))()

	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
	setDeadline := func(index int64, date string) {
		req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/issues/%d/deadline", index), map[string]string{"deadline": date})
		session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	}
	// user2/repo1 holds issue #1 and pull #2, neither with a deadline in the fixtures
	deadlines := map[int64]string{1: "2026-10-06", 2: "2026-10-30"}
	for index, date := range deadlines {
		setDeadline(index, date)
	}
	defer func() { // the issue indexer outlives the test database, so leave it as the fixtures had it
		for index := range deadlines {
			setDeadline(index, "")
		}
	}()

	t.Run("shows issues and pulls on their days", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		var links []string
		doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day:not(.is-other-month) .repo-calendar-entry").Each(func(_ int, a *goquery.Selection) {
			links = append(links, a.AttrOr("href", ""))
		})
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"/user2/repo1/issues/1", "/user2/repo1/pulls/2"}, links)
		// a timezone bug would shift an entry into the neighbouring day cell
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-06"]) a.repo-calendar-entry[href="/user2/repo1/issues/1"]`).Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-30"]) a.repo-calendar-entry[href="/user2/repo1/pulls/2"]`).Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-entry.is-pull").Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day.is-today").Length())
	})

	t.Run("a crowded day folds extra entries into +N more", func(t *testing.T) {
		crowded := []int64{1, 2, 4, 5} // issue 1, pull 2, closed issue 4, pull 5
		for _, index := range crowded {
			setDeadline(index, "2026-10-14")
		}
		defer func() {
			for _, index := range crowded {
				setDeadline(index, "")
			}
			setDeadline(1, deadlines[1]) // back to the shared setup
			setDeadline(2, deadlines[2])
		}()
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar?state=all"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		cell := doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-14"])`)
		assert.Equal(t, 3, cell.ChildrenFiltered("a.repo-calendar-entry").Length())
		more := cell.ChildrenFiltered("details.repo-calendar-more")
		assert.Equal(t, 1, more.Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, more.Find(".repo-calendar-more-list a.repo-calendar-entry").Length())
	})

	t.Run("month navigation keeps the filters", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar?month=2026-09&amp;state=all"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		assert.Zero(t, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day:not(.is-other-month) .repo-calendar-entry").Length())
		next, _ := doc.Find(`.list-header a[href*="month=2026-10"]`).First().Attr("href") // the next-month arrow
		assert.Contains(t, next, "month=2026-10")
		assert.Contains(t, next, "state=all")
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-empty").Length())
	})

	t.Run("the issue list links to the calendar", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/issues"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.list-header a[href="/user2/repo1/calendar"]`).Length())
	})

	t.Run("anonymous users", func(t *testing.T) {
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar"), http.StatusOK)
```

```text
// Copyright 2017 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package timeutil

import (
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
)

// TimeStamp defines a timestamp
type TimeStamp int64

var (
	// mockNow is NOT concurrency-safe!!
	mockNow time.Time

	// Used for IsZero, to check if timestamp is the zero time instant.
	timeZeroUnix = time.Time{}.Unix()
)

// MockSet sets the time to a mocked time.Time
func MockSet(now time.Time) func() {
	mockNow = now
	return MockUnset
}

// MockUnset will unset the mocked time.Time
func MockUnset() {
	mockNow = time.Time{}
}

// TimeStampNow returns now int64
func TimeStampNow() TimeStamp {
	if !mockNow.IsZero() {
		return TimeStamp(mockNow.Unix())
	}
	return TimeStamp(time.Now().Unix())
}

// Add adds seconds and return sum
func (ts TimeStamp) Add(seconds int64) TimeStamp {
	return ts + TimeStamp(seconds)
}

// AddDuration adds time.Duration and return sum
func (ts TimeStamp) AddDuration(interval time.Duration) TimeStamp {
	return ts + TimeStamp(interval/time.Second)
}

// Year returns the time's year
func (ts TimeStamp) Year() int {
	return ts.AsTime().Year()
}

// AsTime convert timestamp as time.Time in Local locale
func (ts TimeStamp) AsTime() (tm time.Time) {
	return ts.AsTimeInLocation(setting.DefaultUILocation)
}

// AsLocalTime convert timestamp as time.Time in local location
func (ts TimeStamp) AsLocalTime() time.Time {
	return time.Unix(int64(ts), 0)
}

// AsTimeInLocation convert timestamp as time.Time
```

```markdown
## Observed Behavior

`TestRepoCalendar` failed on the `test-pgsql-shard-1` job of [run 42658314475](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/42658314475/job/129302849931) (Nov 9) with `race detected during execution of test`. Every assertion passed. The race is on `mockNow` in `modules/timeutil/timestamp.go`: the test's deferred `timeutil.MockUnset()` wrote it while an issue indexer worker read it through `TimeStampNow()` (`Milestone.AfterLoad` → `calcDeadlineStatus`). The test's own `setDeadline` cleanup queued that indexer work a moment earlier.

It only shows up on Postgres because the Postgres shards are the only integration jobs built with `-race` (`.github/actions/pgsql-shard/action.yml`).

The cause is wider than this one test. `mockNow` is a plain global, and its comment already says it is "NOT concurrency-safe!!". Background goroutines read it the whole time a test server runs, so every integration test that calls `timeutil.MockSet` has a data race. Run alone under `-race` on sqlite, these all fail every time (5 of 5 runs for `TestRepoCalendar`, 1 of 1 for the others). Their race partner is the EventSource manager (`modules/eventsource/manager_run.go:35`):

- `TestRepoCalendar` (#98)
- `TestRepoICalFeeds` (#100)
- `TestIssueDueDateFilter` (#34)
- `TestUserHeatmap` and `TestHeatmapEndpoints` (upstream tests)

`actions_concurrency_test.go` also calls `MockSet`. I didn't run it alone.

In a full CI run the detector only reports the race when another goroutine happens to read the clock close to a `MockSet` or `MockUnset`, so CI fails at random on whichever PR is unlucky.

## Expected Behavior

A test can mock the clock while the server's background goroutines read it, and `-race` reports nothing. `TimeStampNow()` still returns the mocked time while a mock is set and the real time after it is unset.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out `main` (reproduced at `ee5b49a892`).
2. Run `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=sqlite GOTEST_FLAGS='-race -count=1' make 'test-integration#TestRepoCalendar'`.
3. The output has `WARNING: DATA RACE` (a write in `timeutil.MockSet`, a read in `timeutil.TimeStampNow`) and `--- FAIL: TestRepoCalendar` with `race detected during execution of test`.
4. Swap in `TestRepoICalFeeds`, `TestIssueDueDateFilter`, `TestUserHeatmap` or `TestHeatmapEndpoints` for the same result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a new unit test in `modules/timeutil` where one goroutine calls `MockSet` and `MockUnset` in a loop while another calls `TimeStampNow`, when it runs with `go test -race`, then it fails on `main` and passes with the fix. `test-unit` already runs with `-race`, so CI catches any regression.
- [ ] AC2: Given a mocked time, when `TimeStampNow()` is called, then it returns the mocked Unix time. After `MockUnset()` it returns the real clock again (unit test).
- [ ] AC3: Given the fix, when each test listed under Observed Behavior runs alone with the command in step 2, then all five runs of each pass with no race report.
- [ ] AC4: Given the PR, when `test-pgsql-shard-1` and `test-pgsql-shard-2` run, then neither reports a race in a `MockSet` test. Run links go in the PR.

## Out of Scope

- The `TestMilestoneBurndown/RealLifecycle` failures on Postgres that #181 lists. They were a same-second ordering bug, fixed in f5c361f00c on Oct 27. The last one ([40424442743](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40424442743), Oct 27) ran on a branch that didn't have that fix yet, and none of the 15 failed `db-tests` runs since show it.
- Turning on `-race` for the other database jobs. #181 covers CI layout and runtime.
- Other unsynchronised test hooks besides `timeutil`'s mock.

## Additional Information

- CI log: [job 129302849931](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/42658314475/job/129302849931), `chore/showcase2-sonarqube-demo`, Postgres 14, `-race -timeout=40m`, tags `bindata gogit`.
- Local: macOS, Go 1.26.10, sqlite, `ee5b49a892`.
- Upstream `go-gitea/gitea` `main` still has the same `mockNow` code, so the fix could go upstream too.

## Design Decision

**Decision:** Store the mocked time in an `atomic.Int64` holding Unix seconds, with 0 meaning "not mocked", and remove the "NOT concurrency-safe" comment. `TimeStampNow()` is the only reader and it only needs seconds. The `MockSet` and `MockUnset` signatures stay the same, so no caller changes.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Stop mocking the clock in our three tests*: work out dates from the real `time.Now()`, or for the calendar tests pass the month in the URL. That fixes #34, #98 and #100, but the two upstream heatmap tests keep racing. The calendar tests also need a fixed "today" to check the `is-today` cell and the default month.
- *Wait for the issue indexer queue to drain before `MockUnset` in each test.* This fixes the Nov 9 race only. The EventSource manager reads the clock on its own ticker, so the race is still there, and every new `MockSet` test would have to remember the wait.
- *Guard `mockNow` with a `sync.RWMutex`.* Also correct, but every `TimeStampNow()` call in production would take a lock, where an atomic load costs about the same as reading the plain variable.

**Rationale:** The defect is in the shared helper, so fixing it there clears every current and future caller in one small change that could also go upstream.

**Consequences:** `modules/timeutil` gains a `sync/atomic` import. A mocked time is still global, so a test that mocks the clock still sees it in background goroutines, exactly as it does today. The difference is that `-race` stops reporting it. Sub-second precision of a mocked `time.Time` is dropped, which `TimeStampNow` already threw away.

## Scope

small (`scope: small`). One helper file and one unit test, plus re-running the five affected integration tests. Nothing changes in production behaviour.
```

The course site doesn't say outright. It says "one of your issues may be a hardening issue" (D1, Sprint 3 page, checked just now). I read that as a cap on how many hardening issues count toward your D1 load, not a ban on having more. A second one is allowed as extra work but probably won't count toward the 2-medium minimum.

So for load:

- **Hardening slot:** #181 (medium) already fills it.
- **Feature work:** #155 is small.
- **The race bug:** it would be a second hardening issue, so it likely adds nothing to your load. It could still go in the report's Suite health section. The site says "fixing [pre-existing failures] is optional (and can be a hardening issue)".

If you need it to count, ask the TA on Zulip whether a second hardening issue counts when a student is below the minimum. Otherwise, a small feature issue is the safe way to make up the gap. Whichever you choose, the bug report is still worth posting, because it explains a CI failure that will keep hitting PRs at random.

```markdown
## Problem

`main`'s CI status means nothing, `main` skips most of the test suites, and backend PRs are slow for a reason we can fix.

### Main is red on every push, so real failures go unnoticed

- `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its runs since the fork (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec`. `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh:33` reads the newest tag with `%(tag)`, which is empty for lightweight tags, and all our `v1.27.3-csci435-*` tags are lightweight. Even with annotated tags it would fail at publish, because the repo has no Snap Store credentials and the `gitea` snap name belongs to upstream.
- `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). Its jobs need upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners. The next push cancels each run, or GitHub drops it after 24 hours in the queue.
- `release-tag-version` matches `v1.*`, so it has run for every sprint tag, and all three runs were cancelled after sitting queued for those runners: s0 ([35251424595](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/35251424595)), s1 ([37872246874](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/37872246874)) and s2 ([40956082407](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40956082407)). The s3 tag will do the same.
- The noise is hiding a real failure. `db-tests` failed on `main` after two docs-only merges ([43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430), [43296442804](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43296442804)) with the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test from #171. Nobody noticed, because every `main` commit was already red.

### Main never runs most of the test suites

Every integration job in `pull-db-tests.yml` has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (lines 20, 56, 91, 188, 236), and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` runs only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` (Go unit tests and Vitest coverage) and nothing else. Since PRs don't have to be up to date with `main` before merging, two PRs that each pass can break `main` together, and no integration or e2e run would show it. The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, so D8's Suite health section has no CI baseline to quote.

### Backend PRs take about 28 minutes, mostly compiling and waiting

Full backend `db-tests` runs take 23.3 to 30.1 min, with a median of about 27.6 (e.g. [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). Waiting for a runner isn't the cause: the median wait is 2 seconds. The time goes to three things:

- The build cache is stale. `cache-seeder` has run once ([40807939468](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40807939468), Oct 29), because it only triggers when `go.sum`, `.golangci.yml` or the cache files change. Its `gobuild-<go.sum hash>` key can never be overwritten, so the cache is now 141 commits behind `main`. It also warms the `-race` build but not `-race -cover`. As a result, each `test-unit` pass spends about 3.6 minutes compiling before the first package result, and every other Go test job compiles more than it should too.
- The two unit-test passes run one after the other. `test-unit` runs the normal pass (9.6 to 12.1 min) and then the `gogit` pass (9.4 to 11.5 min).
- `sonarqube` waits on `test-unit`. It has `needs: test-unit` and runs the Vitest coverage itself, so it can't start until both unit passes are done.

## Goal

`main` is green unless one of our own suites failed, it runs the integration and e2e suites after every merge and on every sprint tag, and anyone can run them against any ref. Backend PRs get the same checks as now, every database included, in noticeably less time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then `release-nightly` and `release-nightly-snapcraft` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued). Given a pushed `v1.*` tag, `release-tag-version` shows as skipped. `release-tag-rc` only triggers on `v1*-rc*` tags, which the course never pushes, so its guard is checked in the diff. Every job in the four workflows has the skip condition, with a same-line comment citing #181 and saying the workflow only runs upstream.
- [ ] AC2: Given any merge to `main`, docs-only ones included, when CI runs, then sqlite, MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres migration plus integration tests, Go unit tests, Vitest and the Playwright e2e suite all run against the merged commit. A newer merge never cancels a run that has already started. If several merges land while a run is in progress, only the newest waiting run is kept: the suites then run against the newest merged commit, and the replaced run shows as cancelled, never failed.
- [ ] AC3: Given a team member opens Actions → `db-tests` or `e2e-tests` → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), or someone pushes a `v*-csci435-*` tag, when the run finishes, then the suites from AC2 have run against that ref. A tag run or manual run never replaces a `main` run and is never replaced by one.
- [ ] AC4: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then the Go build cache is saved again under a key tied to that commit and includes the `-race -cover` build. Given a backend PR branched from `main` after that save, with no Go changes under `modules/` or `models/` (changes there recompile most of the tree whatever the cache holds), when `test-unit`'s normal pass runs, then the first package result appears at most 1 minute after `make test-backend` starts (about 3.6 minutes now).
- [ ] AC5: Given a backend PR, when `db-tests` runs, then the normal and `gogit` unit-test passes run as two separate jobs at the same time. Both run `make test-check`, and only the normal pass uploads Go coverage.
- [ ] AC6: Given any `db-tests` run, when it runs, then Vitest coverage runs in its own job, at the same time as the Go unit tests. `sonarqube` scans both coverage reports, and a failing Vitest test still makes the `db-tests` run fail. `sonarqube` runs only on pull requests and pushes to `main`, and is skipped on tag pushes and manual runs, so an old ref never replaces `main`'s analysis in SonarQube Cloud.
- [ ] AC7: Given the first attempt of four backend PR runs after the fix (a backend PR is one where `files-changed` reports `backend == 'true'`; re-runs don't count), when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` (from the run being created to its last job finishing, runner queue time included) is at most 22 minutes (about 27.6 now), and every job that ran on a backend PR before this change still runs. No database, `-race` or `gogit` coverage is removed. Only runs where no job waited more than 1 minute for a runner count toward the four, so the median doesn't depend on whether a `main` run was using the org's 20 job slots at the time. A run that did wait is replaced by the next backend PR run and listed with its wait time.
- [ ] AC8: Given `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`, then every job with steps has a job-level `timeout-minutes` of at most 60, so a hung job stops there instead of at GitHub's 6-hour default. The `files-changed` jobs are exempt: they call a reusable workflow, where GitHub doesn't allow `timeout-minutes`, and its `detect` job already has a 3-minute timeout.

## Out of Scope

- Fixing the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test. That's #171. This issue makes sure such a failure turns `main` red where people will see it.
- The Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown/RealLifecycle` ([38276920412](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/38276920412) and two other branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` ([42658314475](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/42658314475)). The burndown one was a same-second ordering bug, already fixed in f5c361f00c. The calendar one is a data race in `timeutil.MockSet`, tracked in #185.
- Making status checks required, and protecting tags with a ruleset. Both need repo-admin rights. I'll propose them to the TA once AC2 is green, with one combined check job as the required check, because a skipped job counts as passing.
- Writing each suite's pass/fail/skip counts to the job summary, speeding up `lint-backend` (11 to 12 min, runs alongside the tests), and making individual integration tests faster (#37).

## Open Questions

None open. The one question, whether a 20-minute median was the right target for AC7, was settled on 2026-11-13 by measuring existing runs, and AC7 now says 22 minutes.

- **Fresh cache against stale cache.** The two backend PR runs from Oct 29, within a day of the only `cache-seeder` run ([40897202041](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40897202041), [40897180193](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40897180193)), took 19.8 and 16.7 min. The 14 successful backend PR runs from Nov 11 to 13 have a median of 28.8 min.
- **Where a database job's time goes.** From the job logs, compiling (`make backend`, the migration test binary and the integration test binary) takes 3.9 to 6.8 min per job with the stale cache and 0.8 to 1.3 min with a fresh one. The tests themselves take 9.4 to 12.3 min either way. With no compile time at all, MySQL and MSSQL still need 16 to 17 min each: about 3 for setup, 1 for migrations and 12 for tests.
- **Projection.** Taking each of the 14 recent runs, replacing its compile time with the fresh-cache figure and splitting the unit passes gives a median of 19.8 min, with 5 of the 14 over 20 and 2 over 22. The slowest job is a database job every time (MySQL 7 runs, MSSQL 5, sqlite 1, Postgres shard 1 once); unit tests plus `sonarqube` finish at 15 to 17.5 min.
- **Why 22 and not 20.** A 20-minute median would pass or fail on runner luck: MySQL alone ranged from 16.5 to 27.2 min on the same cache. Reaching 20 reliably means splitting both MySQL and MSSQL, since they take turns being slowest, which adds two jobs per PR against the org's limit of 20.
- **Limits of the measurement.** Only two fresh-cache runs exist, they predate `-cover`, and the suite has grown from about 720 to 729 integration tests since.

## Evidence of Fix

Broken or missing CI check: links to runs before and after.
- **Before:** the runs linked under Problem, and the backend `db-tests` times (median about 27.6 min) with the compile time from [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133).
- **After:**
  - the first push to `main` after the merge, with release workflows skipped (AC1), every suite run (AC2) and the cache saved (AC4);
  - a manual run against `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (AC3);
  - four backend PR runs with their times, their median and each job's compile time (AC4 to AC7);
  - the diff showing a job-level `timeout-minutes` on every job in the three files (AC8).

Every After item needs the change on `main`, so the PR's Test Evidence lists them as manual, post-merge checks, and the results go in a comment on this issue. The s3 tag push (`release-tag-version` skipped, suites run) only happens at the D9 release, after this issue closes, so it gets a follow-up comment here and isn't part of the closing evidence.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.
- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.
**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. Every database job still runs on every backend PR.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`.* Rejected because the Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown` (three branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` came from `services/issue` and `routers/`, outside those paths, so they would have reached `main` without any warning.
- *Drop `-race` or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
- *Only add more shards.* It uses more runners for the same work, so PRs would start waiting on each other because of the org's limit of 20 jobs at once.
**Rationale:** Most of the extra time goes to compiling and to jobs waiting on each other. Fixing that shortens the run and keeps every check. Moving Vitest saves almost no time by itself: across the 14 backend PR runs from Nov 11 to 13, the `frontend-coverage` step took about 6 seconds and the whole `sonarqube` job a median of 2.9 min. The time saving comes from the cache and from splitting the unit passes. Vitest moves so that a failing frontend test shows up in the first minutes of a run; today it runs inside `sonarqube`, which waits for both unit passes, about 25 minutes in.
**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 22-minute target is limited by the slowest database job, which is MySQL or MSSQL in most runs.

### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed

**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Only PR jobs restore with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry. The seeder never restores an older build cache and always builds clean, so an entry holds one commit's build and doesn't grow from save to save. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.
- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.
**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.
**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. The `gomod` and `golint` caches share that limit, so eviction can drop them too and slow `lint-backend` and module downloads. One extra seeder run per merge. A clean seeder build takes about 30 min (the Oct 29 run did), which no PR waits on; when merges come in a burst the newer seeder run cancels the older one, so the cache can lag until the last one finishes. The 2.25 GB is today's size without the `-race -cover` build, which will add to it and isn't measured yet.

### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. Pushes to `main` share one concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress` false, so a running job is never cancelled. Each tag and each manual run gets its own group, so it neither waits on nor replaces a `main` run. Pull request runs keep the group they have now.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.
- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.
- *Keep the `files-changed` filter on pushes to `main`, so docs-only merges skip the suites.* Most merges here are docs-only, and the two `db-tests` failures linked under Problem both came after docs-only merges, so repeat runs on an unchanged tree are how a flaky test shows up. Replacing the waiting run caps the cost at one queued run.
**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.
**Consequences:** About 12 jobs per merge on `main` (10 in `db-tests`, 2 in `e2e-tests`), plus the two `cache-seeder` jobs. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge, and the replaced run shows as cancelled on its commit; that saves runner time against the org's limit of 20 jobs. Every suite still `needs: files-changed`, so on push, tag and manual runs that job has to succeed (or be bypassed) even when it has no base to compare against, or every suite is skipped. A manual run takes the workflow file from `main` but `.github/actions/*` and the Makefile from the ref it checks out. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` has the same actions and make targets as `main`; a ref from before those existed may not run.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml`, `pull-compliance.yml` (timeouts), `cache-seeder.yml`, the `go-cache` action and the four release workflows. No product code changes. Evidence needs several pushes to `main`, a tag push, a manual run against a tag and four timed PR runs, each checked against the before numbers.
```

```text
const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence
const enabledSettingKey = 'keyboard-shortcuts-enabled';

export type Shortcut = {

};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick&lt;Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section' | 'alwaysOn'&gt;;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;
  // kept in memory as well, so the switch works for this page even where storage throws

  isEnabled(): boolean {
    return this.enabled;
  }

  setEnabled(enabled: boolean) {
    this.enabled = enabled;
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    localUserSettings.setBoolean(enabledSettingKey, enabled);
  }

    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one

    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section, alwaysOn}) =&gt; ({keys, description, section, alwaysOn}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

import {replaceTextareaSelection} from './comp/EditorMarkdown.ts';
import {showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import type {ComboMarkdownEditor} from './comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts';

/** the backtick fence for a suggestion holding `line`: longer than any backtick run in it, at least 3 */
export function suggestionFence(line: string): string {
  let longest = 0;
  for (const run of line.match(/`+/g) ?? []) longest = Math.max(longest, run.length);
  return '`'.repeat(Math.max(3, longest + 1));
}

/** the text to insert after `textBefore` (the textarea text before the selection),
 *  and the offset in it where the cursor goes: the end of `line` inside the block */
export function buildSuggestionInsert(textBefore: string, line: string): {text: string, cursor: number} {
  const fence = suggestionFence(line);
  const prefix = textBefore &amp;&amp; !textBefore.endsWith('\n') ? '\n' : ''; // the block starts on a line of its own
  const head = `${prefix}${fence}suggestion\n${line}`;
  return {text: `${head}\n${fence}\n`, cursor: head.length};
}

/** where to insert a block for a cursor at `pos`: after the fenced code block holding `pos`, if any, so a
 *  block is never nested in another (CommonMark: a closing fence uses the opening's character, is at least
 *  as long and has no info string; an unclosed block runs to the end) */
export function suggestionInsertPos(value: string, pos: number): number {
  let open: {char: string, len: number} | null = null;
  let lineStart = 0;
  while (true) {
    const newline = value.indexOf('\n', lineStart);
    const lineEnd = newline === -1 ? value.length : newline;
    const fence = /^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/.exec(value.slice(lineStart, lineEnd));
    if (!open) {
      if (pos &lt;= lineStart) return pos;
      if (fence &amp;&amp; !(fence[1][0] === '`' &amp;&amp; fence[2].includes('`'))) {
        open = {char: fence[1][0], len: fence[1].length};
      } else if (pos &lt;= lineEnd) {
        return pos;
      }
    } else if (fence?.[1][0] === open.char &amp;&amp; fence[1].length &gt;= open.len &amp;&amp; !fence[2].trim()) {
      if (pos &lt;= lineEnd) return newline === -1 ? value.length : newline + 1;
      open = null;
    }
    if (newline === -1) return open ? value.length : pos;
    lineStart = newline + 1;
  }
}

/** the range a block replaces for a selection from `start` to `end`: the selection itself (AC2), or, when
 *  either end is inside a fenced block, an empty range after that block, so no block is cut into */
export function suggestionInsertRange(value: string, start: number, end: number): [number, number] {
  const afterEnd = suggestionInsertPos(value, end);
  if (afterEnd !== end) return [afterEnd, afterEnd];
  const afterStart = suggestionInsertPos(value, start);
  if (afterStart !== start) return [afterStart, afterStart];
  return [start, end];
}
```

```text
Out of Scope

- Selecting several lines (S5).
- Rendering the block as a diff (S1) and applying it (S3).
- The button in reply forms of an existing conversation. A line that already has a conversation
  has no `+`, so suggestions there wait for a later issue.
- The legacy EasyMDE editor: switching to it hides the button, and switching back shows it again.
- Server-side checks on suggestion blocks. The server stores them as plain markdown.

### Open Questions

- Customer question 5 on #151: are suggestions on the old (deleted) side allowed? AC6 assumes no.
- New question for the customer: should a reviewer be able to write a suggestion on a merged or
  closed PR, where it can never be applied? AC9 assumes yes, since the form is already there.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Read the line text from the diff row already in the DOM (the `.code-inner` cell of
the row the form belongs to, as `textContent`) and insert it with the existing
`replaceTextareaSelection` helper from `EditorMarkdown.ts`; no server call. The button is added to
the shared markdown toolbar only when the editor sits inside a code comment form for the right
side.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fetch the raw line from the server.* Exact, but a round trip for text already on the page, and a
  new endpoint with its own permission checks.
- *Server-render the block into the form's initial value.* Forces a suggestion on every comment and
  the reviewer has to delete it for a plain comment.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-15 07:01:16Z)**_

Yes. The best fit is a gap you left yourself in #155: the **"Suggest change" button doesn't appear in reply forms**. Your S2 spec deferred it:

> The button in reply forms of an existing conversation. A line that already has a conversation has no `+`, so suggestions there wait for a later issue.

S3 (#156) can already apply a suggestion written in a reply ("in a review comment or a reply in its thread", AC1). On a line that already has a conversation, the only way to suggest a change today is to type the fenced block by hand.

Why it fits:

- **It counts toward your load.** It would be S8, a sub-issue of #151, and those count. It's not hardening, so the one-hardening limit doesn't apply.
- **It's small and mostly reuse.** `initSuggestChangeButton`, `suggestionInsertRange` and the fence logic in `web_src/js/features/repo-diff-suggestion.ts` stay as they are. The new work is finding the thread's line in reply forms and showing the button there.
- **It doesn't wait on the customer.** It builds on S2's assumption that suggestions only go on new-side lines.
- **It fits the deadline if you move fast.** It needs a spec review and a merged PR by Nov 19, so post the spec today.

One choice for the spec: limit it to reply forms on the Files tab, or also cover the Conversation tab. The Conversation tab only shows a code snippet, not the diff row, so the line text has to come from somewhere else. I'd keep it to the Files tab and list the Conversation tab as out of scope.

A smaller backup: a keyboard shortcut (say Ctrl+G) that inserts a suggestion from inside the comment box. One catch is that your shortcut registry ignores Ctrl presses and keys typed in a textarea, so it would need its own handler on the textarea. It's also thinner as a feature, so I'd only use it if the reply-form idea falls through.

Want me to draft S8 as a user story, plus a short comment for #151 adding it to the breakdown?

```text
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #154 (S1) and #155 (S2), both merged

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana opens the Files changed tab of a pull request. She clicks the number of new-side line 18,
shift-clicks the number of line 22, then clicks `+` on line 22. The comment form is headed
"Lines 18–22". She clicks "Suggest change", and the block is pre-filled with those five lines. She
rewrites them as three lines and posts. Ben opens the PR and sees a "Suggested change" diff with
five red lines and three green ones. (Applying it is S3 #156.) A keyboard user does the same with
Enter on line 18's number and Shift+Enter on line 22's.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a reviewer clicks the number of new-side line 18 and shift-clicks the number of
  new-side line 22 in the same hunk, when they click `+` on line 22, then the comment form's header
  reads "Lines 18–22"; after posting, the comment's thread appears under line 22 with the header
  "Lines 18–22".
- [ ] AC2: Given a reviewer selects upward (clicks line 22, then shift-clicks line 18), when they
  click `+` on line 22, then the header reads "Lines 18–22" and the comment is saved for lines
  18–22, the same as AC1.
- [ ] AC3: Given a one-line selection (shift-clicking the line already selected, or clicking `+`
  with no selection), when the comment is posted, then it is an ordinary single-line comment with no
  "Lines" header.
- [ ] AC4: Given the comment form for lines 18–22, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then
  the inserted `suggestion` block contains lines 18 to 22 in order, with their indentation kept.
- [ ] AC5: Given a code comment on lines 18–22 whose body has one `suggestion` block of three lines,
  when it is shown in the Files changed or Conversation tab, then the "Suggested change" diff shows
  lines 18 to 22 as five removed (red) lines in order, followed by the three block lines as added
  (green) lines.
- [ ] AC6: Given a code comment on lines 18–22 with an empty `suggestion` block, when it is shown,
  then lines 18 to 22 show as removed and no line shows as added.
- [ ] AC7: Given a code comment on lines 18–22, when a push changes the text of any one line from 18
  to 22 (the first, one in the middle, or the last), then the comment is marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC8: Given a code comment on lines 18–22, when a push changes only lines after line 22, then
  the comment is not marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC9: Given a code comment on a range that ends on the file's last line, when a push deletes
  that last line, or deletes the file, then the comment is marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC10: Given a reviewer has selected a line, when they shift-click a line that would make the
  range cross a hunk header or include expanded context lines, then no range is selected and they
  see "A comment can only cover lines on one side of a single hunk."
- [ ] AC11: Given a reviewer has selected an old-side (deleted) line, when they shift-click a
  new-side line (or the other way round), then no range is selected and they see the same message
  as AC10.
- [ ] AC12: Given a direct POST to the code-comment endpoint whose start line is after its end line,
  is on the old side, or is not in the same hunk as the end line, when it is submitted, then the
  response is 400 with the AC10 message and no comment is saved.
- [ ] AC13: Given single-line code comments created before this change, when they are shown and when
  a push changes their line, then they render and are marked Outdated exactly as before.
- [ ] AC14: Given a keyboard user focuses the number of new-side line 18 and presses Enter, then
  focuses the number of line 22 and presses Shift+Enter, when they activate `+` on line 22, then the
  result is the same as AC1 ("Lines 18–22").
- [ ] AC15: Given a range the server refuses when the form is submitted (for example, one picked
  while the diff ignores whitespace or shows a single commit, so its hunks differ from the full PR
  diff), when the reviewer submits the comment form, then they see the AC10 message, the form stays
  open with their text, and no comment is saved.

### Out of Scope

- Ranges across files.
- Ranges on the old (deleted) side of the diff.
- Applying a range suggestion. S3 #156 (apply) and S6 #159 (apply several) read the stored start
  line to replace exactly the range.
- A start-line field in the REST API: S7 #160.
- Selecting by dragging; only click / shift-click, or Enter / Shift+Enter, on line numbers.
- Ranges that include expanded context lines (lines outside a hunk); they are refused (AC10).
- Following a range when lines are inserted above it. The comment goes Outdated, as single-line
  comments do today.

### Open Questions

- None. The maximum range length is resolved as the size of one hunk, with no separate cap; AC10
  and AC12 enforce it.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Store a range comment's start line as `StartLine` in the comment's existing
`CommentMetaData` JSON field (absent = single-line, as today), and keep `Line` as the range end.

**Alternatives Considered:**

- _A new `start_line` column on `comment`._ Typed and queryable, but needs a migration on Gitea's
  largest table, and the repo convention (`models/issues/comment.go`, `CommentMetaData`) is that
  non-index data goes in the metadata field. Nothing needs to filter by start line in SQL.
- _One linked comment per line._ Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4 #157.

**Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so thread placement (`FetchCodeComments` keys on `Line`),
replies, the API and every existing row are untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads the
start line. Old rows have no `StartLine`, so AC13 holds without a migration.

**Consequences:** No migration. The start line can't be filtered in SQL. S3, S6 and S7 read

      ntr = createElementFromHTML(html`
        &lt;tr class="add-comment" data-line-type="${lineType}"&gt;
          ${isSplit ? htmlRaw(tdSplit) : htmlRaw(tdUnified)}

      td.querySelector&lt;HTMLInputElement&gt;("input[name='line']")!.value = idx;

      td.querySelector&lt;HTMLInputElement&gt;("input[name='path']")!.value = String(path);
      const editor = await initComboMarkdownEditor(td.querySelector&lt;HTMLElement&gt;('.combo-markdown-editor')!);
      // suggestions replace new-side lines only, old-side ones have nothing to apply to
      if (side === 'right') initSuggestChangeButton(editor, codeLine);
      editor.focus();
    }
  });

export function initRepoIssueReferenceIssue() {
  const elDropdown = document.querySelector('.issue_reference_repository_search');
  if (!elDropdown) return;
  const form = elDropdown.closest('form')!;
  fomanticQuery(elDropdown).dropdown({
    fullTextSearch: true,
    apiSettings: {
      cache: false,
      rawResponse: true,
      url: `${appSubUrl}/repo/search?q={query}&amp;limit=20`,
      onResponse(response: any) {
        const filteredResponse = {success: true, results: [] as Array&lt;Record&lt;string, any&gt;&gt;};
        for (const repo of response.data) {
          filteredResponse.results.push({
            name: htmlEscape(repo.repository.full_name),
            value: repo.repository.full_name,
          });
        }
        return filteredResponse;
```

```text
export function initRepoIssueCodeCommentCancel() {
  // Cancel inline code comment
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) =&gt; {
    if (!(e.target as HTMLElement).matches('.cancel-code-comment')) return;

    const form = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('form')!;
    if (form?.classList.contains('comment-form')) {
      hideElem(form);
      showElem(form.closest('.comment-code-cloud')!.querySelectorAll('button.comment-form-reply'));
    } else {
      form.closest('.comment-code-cloud')?.remove();
    }
  });
}

export function initRepoIssueComments() {
  if (!document.querySelector('.repository.view.issue .timeline')) return;

  document.addEventListener('click', (e: Event) =&gt; {
    const urlTarget = document.querySelector(':target');
    if (!urlTarget) return;

    const urlTargetId = urlTarget.id;
    if (!urlTargetId) return;

    if (!/^(issue|pull)(comment)?-\d+$/.test(urlTargetId)) return;

    if (!(e.target as HTMLElement).closest(`#${urlTargetId}`)) {
      // if the user clicks outside the comment, remove the hash from the url
      // use empty hash and state to avoid scrolling
      window.location.hash = ' ';
      window.history.pushState(null, '', ' ');
    }
  });
}

export async function handleReply(el: HTMLElement) {
  const form = el.closest('.comment-code-cloud')!.querySelector('.comment-form')!;
  const textarea = form.querySelector('textarea');

  hideElem(el);
  showElem(form);
  const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(textarea) ?? await initComboMarkdownEditor(form.querySelector('.combo-markdown-editor')!);
  editor.focus();
  return editor;
}
```
