s2head:
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151

As a reviewer, I want a button that fills in a suggestion block with the current line so that I
only edit the code instead of copying it and remembering the syntax.

### User Scenario

Ana opens the Files tab of an open PR and clicks the `+` next to new-side line 18. The code
comment form that opens has a "Suggest change" button in its toolbar. She clicks it and the
textarea gets a ```` ```suggestion ```` block holding line 18's current text, with the cursor at the
end of that line inside the block. She edits the line and clicks "Add single comment". The comment
is saved with the block as she typed it; showing it as a diff is S1's job.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the code comment form opened on a new-side line (an added line, or an unchanged
  context line, including lines revealed by "expand"), in split or unified view, when the reviewer
  clicks "Suggest change", then the textarea contains a block made of a fence line
  ```` ```suggestion ````, the line's exact text (leading tabs and spaces kept, no `+` or space
  diff marker, no highlighting markup), and a closing fence.
- [ ] AC2: Given the textarea already has text, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then the
  block is inserted at the cursor (replacing any selected text), starts on a line of its own and is
  followed by a newline, and the text before and after it is kept.
- [ ] AC3: Given the code comment form, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then the
  textarea has focus and the cursor sits at the end of the line's text inside the block.
- [ ] AC4: Given the line's text contains a run of N backticks with N ≥ 3 (for example
  ```` ```js ````), when the block is inserted, then both fences use N+1 backticks, so the block
  is not closed early. With fewer than 3 backticks in a row, the fences stay at 3.
- [ ] AC5: Given an empty or whitespace-only line, when the block is inserted, then the block
  holds that line as is (an empty line or the same whitespace) between the fences.
- [ ] AC6: Given the form opened on an old-side line (a deleted line, or the left column of a
  changed line in split view), when the form is shown, then the "Suggest change" button is not
  shown. If the customer's answer to question 5 on #151 allows old-side suggestions, this AC is
  updated before coding starts.
- [ ] AC7: Given any markdown editor other than the code comment form (issue or PR conversation
  comment, review summary, editing an existing comment, a reply in an existing conversation), when
  it is shown, then it has no "Suggest change" button.
- [ ] AC8: Given a visitor who is not signed in, or a repository that is archived, when the Files
  tab is shown, then there is no code comment form and so no button (behaviour unchanged,
  regression test).
- [ ] AC9: Given a merged or closed PR, when the reviewer opens the code comment form, then the
  button is shown and works as in AC1 (Gitea still allows code comments there). If the customer
  answers that suggestions on closed PRs should be blocked, this AC is updated before coding.
- [ ] AC10: The button is a keyboard-focusable `&lt;button&gt;` with an accessible name and tooltip
  from a new locale key `repo.diff.comment.suggest_change` (English "Suggest change", added to
  `locale_en-US.json` only).
- [ ] AC11: Given a comment with a suggestion block, when it is submitted, then the stored comment
  content is exactly the textarea text</result>
</event>
```

`````markdown
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #155 (S2), merged

As a reviewer replying in an existing conversation on a pull request's code, I want the same "Suggest change" button the new-comment form has, so that I can propose a fix on a line that already has a thread without typing the suggestion block by hand.

### User Scenario

Ben opens the Files tab of an open PR. Line 18 already has a thread where Ana asked "should this be `>=`?". Ben clicks Reply under that thread, and the reply form has a "Suggest change" button in its toolbar. He clicks it, the textarea gets a ```` ```suggestion ```` block holding line 18's current text, and he changes `>` to `>=` and clicks Reply. His reply shows as a suggested change (S1), and the PR author can apply it (S3 #156, which already accepts suggestions in replies).

S2 (#155) left this out on purpose: a line that already has a conversation has no `+`, so today the only way to suggest a change there is to type the fenced block by hand.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a conversation on a new-side line in the Files tab, in split or unified view, when the reviewer clicks Reply and then "Suggest change", then the reply textarea gets the same block S2 inserts for that line (#155 AC1 to AC5 and AC12: exact line text, fence length, insertion at the cursor, cursor placement, no second block nested in the first).
- [ ] AC2: Given a conversation on an old-side line (a deleted line, or the left column in split view), when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button, matching #155 AC6. If the customer allows old-side suggestions (question 5 on #151), this AC follows whatever S2 changes to.
- [ ] AC3: Given a conversation marked Outdated, when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button. The diff row under it shows the line as it is now, not the line the thread was written on, and S3 would refuse to apply the suggestion anyway (#156 AC3).
- [ ] AC4: Given the reviewer clicks Reply, then Cancel, then Reply again on the same conversation, when they click "Suggest change" once, then exactly one block is inserted. Reopening the form does not attach a second handler.
- [ ] AC5: Given a reply form in the Conversation tab, or any editor S2's AC7 lists other than the Files tab reply form, when it is shown, then it has no "Suggest change" button. #155 AC7's test is updated so that only the Files tab reply case changes.
- [ ] AC6: Given a reply with a suggestion block, when it is submitted, then the stored reply content is exactly the textarea text and the reply joins the same conversation (same review, path and line) as before this change.
- [ ] AC7: Given a visitor who is not signed in, or an archived repository, when the Files tab is shown, then there is no Reply button and so no "Suggest change" button (behaviour unchanged, regression test).
- [ ] AC8: Given a conversation whose root comment covers several lines (S5 #158), when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button, since a one-line block would only cover the range's last line. If #158 merges after this issue, #158's PR adds this check; if before, this PR does.
- [ ] AC9: The button in the reply form is the same keyboard-focusable `<button>` as in S2, with the same accessible name and tooltip (`repo.diff.comment.suggest_change`). No new locale key.

### Out of Scope

- The Conversation tab. Its code snippet comes from the comment's stored patch rather than a diff row, so reading the line there needs different code. A later issue can add it.
- Multi-line suggestions in replies to range conversations (S5 #158 or a follow-up).
- Editing an existing comment to add a suggestion.
- Server-side checks on suggestion blocks. The server stores replies as plain markdown, as in S2.

### Open Questions

None. Old-side lines follow customer question 5 through S2 (AC2).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** In the Files tab, read the line text from the diff row the conversation sits under (the row before its `tr.add-comment`, using the conversation holder's `data-side`), and call S2's `initSuggestChangeButton` once, when the reply form's editor is first created in `handleReply`. The template's `"SuggestChange" (not $.reply)` becomes "not a reply, or a reply on the Files tab".

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Render the line text into the conversation template on the server*, from the comment's stored patch. That would also work in the Conversation tab and gives the text the thread was written on. But it is a Go and template change for text already on the page in the Files tab, and the stored patch line and the current head line can differ, which raises the outdated question S3 already handles.
- *Show the `+` on lines that already have a conversation*, so a reviewer starts a new thread with S2's existing button. Gitea's diff puts one conversation per line and side in a single `add-comment` row, so a second thread on the same line changes how threads are placed and loaded, which is far more than a small issue.

**Rationale:** It reuses S2's insert code and tests as they are and only changes where the button is turned on. The row the line text comes from is the same one S2 reads, so both forms produce the same block for the same line.

**Consequences:** No server change. The Conversation tab still has no button until a follow-up. `handleReply` has to tell a Files tab reply form apart from a Conversation tab one, and has to init the button only once per form (AC4).

### Scope

small (`scope: small`). One template condition and a few lines in `handleReply` (`web_src/js/features/repo-issue.ts`), plus Vitest cases and one Playwright test for the reply flow. All of the insert logic is S2's and stays as it is.

`````

### User Scenario

Ben clicks Reply under that thread, and the reply form has a "Suggest change" button in its toolbar. He clicks it, the textarea gets a ```` ```suggestion ```` block holding line 18's current text, and he changes `&gt;` to `&gt;=` and clicks Reply. His reply shows as a suggested change (S1), and the PR author can apply it (S3 #156, which already accepts suggestions in replies).

S2 (#155) left this out on purpose: a line that already has a conversation has no `+`, so today the only way to suggest a change there is to type the fenced block by hand.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a conversation on a new-side line in the Files tab, in split or unified view, when the reviewer clicks Reply and then "Suggest change", then the reply textarea gets the same block S2 inserts for that line (#155 AC1 to AC5 and AC12: exact line text, fence length, insertion at the cursor, cursor placement, no second block nested in the first).
- [ ] AC2: Given a conversation on an old-side line (a deleted line, or the left column in split view), when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button, matching #155 AC6. - [ ] AC3: Given the Files tab shows outdated comments (`show-outdated=true`) and a conversation is marked Outdated, when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button. The diff row under it shows the line as it is now, not the line the thread was written on, and S3 would refuse to apply the suggestion anyway (#156 AC3).
- [ ] AC4: Given the reviewer clicks Reply, then Cancel, then Reply again on the same conversation, when they click "Suggest change" once, then exactly one block is inserted. Reopening the form does not attach a second handler.
- [ ] AC5: Given a reply form in the Conversation tab, or any editor S2's AC7 lists other than the Files tab reply form, when it is shown, then it has no "Suggest change" button. #155 AC7's test is updated so that only the Files tab reply case changes.
- [ ] AC6: Given a reply with a suggestion block, when it is submitted, then the stored reply content is exactly the textarea text and the reply joins the same conversation (same review, path and line) as before this change.
- [ ] AC7: Given a visitor who is not signed in, or an archived repository, when the Files tab is shown, then there is no Reply button and so no "Suggest change" button (behaviour unchanged, regression test).
- [ ] AC8: Given a conversation whose root comment covers several lines (S5 #158), when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button, since a one-line block would only cover the range's last line. If #158 merges after this issue, #158's PR adds this check; if before, this PR does.
- [ ] AC9: The button in the reply form is the same keyboard-focusable `&lt;button&gt;` as in S2, with the same accessible name and tooltip (`repo.diff.comment.suggest_change`). No new locale key.

### Out of Scope

- The Conversation tab. Its code snippet comes from the comment's stored patch rather than a diff row, so reading the line there needs different code. A later issue can add it.
- Multi-line suggestions in replies to range conversations (S5 #158 or a follow-up).
- Editing an existing comment to add a suggestion.
- Server-side checks on suggestion blocks. The server stores replies as plain markdown, as in S2.

### Open Questions

None. Old-side lines follow customer question 5 through S2 (AC2).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** In the Files tab, read the line text from the diff row the conversation sits under (the row before its `tr.add-comment`, using the conversation holder's `data-side`), and call S2's `initSuggestChangeButton` once, when the reply form's editor is first created in `handleReply`. The template's `"SuggestChange" (not $.reply)` becomes "not a reply, or a reply on the Files tab".

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Render the line text into the conversation template on the server*, from the comment's stored patch. That would also work in the Conversation tab and gives the text the thread was written on. But it is a Go and template change for text already on the page in the Files tab, and the stored patch line and the current head line can differ, which raises the outdated question S3 already handles.
- *Show the `+` on lines that already have a conversation*, so a reviewer starts a new thread with S2's existing button. Gitea's diff puts one conversation per line and side in a single `add-comment` row, so a second thread on the same line changes how threads are placed and loaded, which is far more than a small issue.

**Rationale:** It reuses S2's insert code and tests as they are and only changes where the button is turned on. The row the line text comes from is the same one S2 reads, so both forms produce the same block for the same line.

**Consequences:** No server change. The Conversation tab still has no button until a follow-up. `handleReply` has to tell a Files tab reply form apart from a Conversation tab one, and has to init the button only once per form (AC4).

### Scope

small (`scope: small`). One template condition and a few lines in `handleReply` (`web_src/js/features/repo-issue.ts`), plus Vitest cases and one Playwright test for the reply flow. All of the insert logic is S2's and stays as it is.

**Title:** S8. Add the "Suggest change" button to reply forms in the Files tab

````markdown
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #155 (S2), merged

As a reviewer replying in an existing conversation on a pull request's code, I want the same "Suggest change" button the new-comment form has, so that I can propose a fix on a line that already has a thread without typing the suggestion block by hand.

### User Scenario

Ben opens the Files tab of an open PR. Line 18 already has a thread where Ana asked "should this be `>=`?". Ben clicks Reply under that thread, and the reply form has a "Suggest change" button in its toolbar. He clicks it, the textarea gets a ```` ```suggestion ```` block holding line 18's current text, and he changes `>` to `>=` and clicks Reply. His reply shows as a suggested change (S1), and the PR author can apply it (S3 #156, which already accepts suggestions in replies).

S2 (#155) left this out on purpose: a line that already has a conversation has no `+`, so today the only way to suggest a change there is to type the fenced block by hand.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a conversation on a new-side line in the Files tab, in split or unified view, when the reviewer clicks Reply and then "Suggest change", then the reply textarea gets the same block S2 inserts for that line (#155 AC1 to AC5 and AC12: exact line text, fence length, insertion at the cursor, cursor placement, no second block nested in the first).
- [ ] AC2: Given a conversation on an old-side line (a deleted line, or the left column in split view), when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button, matching #155 AC6. If the customer allows old-side suggestions (question 5 on #151), this AC follows whatever S2 changes to.
- [ ] AC3: Given the Files tab shows outdated comments (`show-outdated=true`) and a conversation is marked Outdated, when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button. The diff row under it shows the line as it is now, not the line the thread was written on, and S3 would refuse to apply the suggestion anyway (#156 AC3).
- [ ] AC4: Given the reviewer clicks Reply, then Cancel, then Reply again on the same conversation, when they click "Suggest change" once, then exactly one block is inserted. Reopening the form does not attach a second handler.
- [ ] AC5: Given a reply form in the Conversation tab, or any editor S2's AC7 lists other than the Files tab reply form, when it is shown, then it has no "Suggest change" button. #155 AC7's test is updated so that only the Files tab reply case changes.
- [ ] AC6: Given a reply with a suggestion block, when it is submitted, then the stored reply content is exactly the textarea text and the reply joins the same conversation (same review, path and line) as before this change.
- [ ] AC7: Given a visitor who is not signed in, or an archived repository, when the Files tab is shown, then there is no Reply button and so no "Suggest change" button (behaviour unchanged, regression test).
- [ ] AC8: Given a conversation whose root comment covers several lines (S5 #158), when the reviewer clicks Reply, then the reply form has no "Suggest change" button, since a one-line block would only cover the range's last line. If #158 merges after this issue, #158's PR adds this check; if before, this PR does.
- [ ] AC9: The button in the reply form is the same keyboard-focusable `<button>` as in S2, with the same accessible name and tooltip (`repo.diff.comment.suggest_change`). No new locale key.

### Out of Scope

- The Conversation tab. Its code snippet comes from the comment's stored patch rather than a diff row, so reading the line there needs different code. A later issue can add it.
- Multi-line suggestions in replies to range conversations (S5 #158 or a follow-up).
- Editing an existing comment to add a suggestion.
- Server-side checks on suggestion blocks. The server stores replies as plain markdown, as in S2.

### Open Questions

None. Old-side lines follow customer question 5 through S2 (AC2).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** In the Files tab, read the line text from the diff row the conversation sits under (the row before its `tr.add-comment`, using the conversation holder's `data-side`), and call S2's `initSuggestChangeButton` once, when the reply form's editor is first created in `handleReply`. The template's `"SuggestChange" (not $.reply)` becomes "not a reply, or a reply on the Files tab".

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Render the line text into the conversation template on the server*, from the comment's stored patch. That would also work in the Conversation tab and gives the text the thread was written on. But it is a Go and template change for text already on the page in the Files tab, and the stored patch line and the current head line can differ, which raises the outdated question S3 already handles.
- *Show the `+` on lines that already have a conversation*, so a reviewer starts a new thread with S2's existing button. Gitea's diff puts one conversation per line and side in a single `add-comment` row, so a second thread on the same line changes how threads are placed and loaded, which is far more than a small issue.

**Rationale:** It reuses S2's insert code and tests as they are and only changes where the button is turned on. The row the line text comes from is the same one S2 reads, so both forms produce the same block for the same line.

**Consequences:** No server change. The Conversation tab still has no button until a follow-up. `handleReply` has to tell a Files tab reply form apart from a Conversation tab one, and has to init the button only once per form (AC4).

### Scope

small (`scope: small`). One template condition and a few lines in `handleReply` (`web_src/js/features/repo-issue.ts`), plus Vitest cases and one Playwright test for the reply flow. All of the insert logic is S2's and stays as it is.
